title: Python SDK: implement standardized retry policy (backoff+jitter, Retry-After) + consistent retryable error typing
creator: Ibrahim Khan
body:
## Context
Python SDK currently has retry behavior that diverges from TS/Go (especially around 429 handling, network errors, and Retry-After). This ticket implements the v1 standard retry policy in `redwood-sdk-python` and ensures errors are typed/annotated consistently so callers can make correct decisions (retry vs fail fast) and Support can triage quickly using request_id.

This work is part of the SDK parity initiative (auth/retry/timeout/streaming). Streaming-specific retries are intentionally conservative and are handled in separate work; this ticket focuses on non-streaming request paths plus shared retry utilities.

## Goals / acceptance criteria
- Default retry policy matches `sdk-retry-timeout-standard` and ADR `adr-sdk-retry-policy-v1`.
- Retries occur for:
  - HTTP 429 (rate limited), respecting `Retry-After` when present
  - HTTP 5xx (gateway/service errors)
  - Selected transient network errors (connect reset, DNS, TLS handshake, read timeout at transport layer)
- No retries for:
  - 4xx client errors like 400/401/403/404/422 (explicitly)
  - 408 only if surfaced as a true gateway timeout (treated as retryable in standard); do not retry application-level timeouts that are user-configured cancellations
- Retry-After parsing supports both delta-seconds and HTTP-date formats; invalid values are ignored safely.
- Exponential backoff with jitter; caps aligned with standard; no thundering herd behavior.
- Errors raised by the SDK include:
  - `request_id` (when present)
  - `status_code`
  - `error_code` (gateway enum when available)
  - `retryable` boolean (SDK classification)
  - `retry_after_ms` (when known)
- Conformance tests/fixtures cover key cases (429 + Retry-After, 503, network error classification, max attempts).

## Implementation summary
### 1) Retry middleware / request wrapper (PR #846)
- Added a single retry wrapper around HTTP execution path used by all non-streaming endpoints.
- Default policy (as shipped):
  - `max_attempts`: 4 (1 initial + up to 3 retries)
  - `base_delay_ms`: 250
  - `max_delay_ms`: 8000
  - Backoff: exponential with jitter ("full jitter" variant): sleep = random(0, min(max_delay, base_delay * 2^attempt))
  - Respect `Retry-After`: yes (default). When present and parseable, it overrides backoff sleep for 429 (and can override for 503 if gateway sends it).
  - Per-attempt timeout: delegated to the timeout model ticket (ENG-512x). This implementation ensures retry sleep does not consume request timeout budget (i.e., overall timeout semantics handled at caller layer).

- Retryable conditions:
  - HTTP status codes: 429, 500, 502, 503, 504
  - 408: retryable only if server response code is 408 (not a client-side timeout exception)
  - Network exceptions: httpx transport errors consistent with standard (ConnectError, ReadError, RemoteProtocolError). We explicitly do NOT retry on user cancellation (CancelledError) or on validation/serialization errors.

- Guardrails:
  - If response includes `idempotency-key` guidance in docs, we do not auto-generate keys in this change (non-goal), but we log a warning in debug mode when retrying a non-idempotent request without an idempotency key configured.
  - Implemented a per-request retry context that tracks attempt number and last exception; prevents infinite loops.

### 2) Retry-After parsing
- Supports:
  - Delta seconds: `Retry-After: 2`
  - HTTP-date: `Retry-After: Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT`
- Parsing behavior:
  - If HTTP-date is in the past, treat as 0ms.
  - If value is unparseable, ignore and fall back to exponential backoff.
  - Cap applied: retry_after_ms <= 30_000ms (cap from standard) to avoid long hangs by default. Users can override cap via config.

### 3) Error taxonomy alignment (partial; full mapping depends on ENG-5126)
- Added/updated error classes to carry consistent fields:
  - `RedwoodAPIError` base: message, request_id, status_code, error_code, retryable, response_headers
  - `RateLimitError` for 429
  - `ServiceUnavailableError` for 503/504
  - `APIConnectionError` for transport/network failures (retryable=true)
- Ensured `request_id` is extracted from:
  - `x-request-id` header (preferred)
  - error JSON payload field `request_id` when present

### 4) Observability hooks
- Added standardized debug logging fields (no telemetry shipment in this PR):
  - request_id
  - attempt
  - retry_count
  - retry_sleep_ms
  - retry_reason (status_code vs exception_type)
- Verified secret redaction in logs (no auth header, no API key in exception repr).

### 5) Conformance coverage (PR #857)
- Added fixtures and a small runner to simulate:
  - 429 with `Retry-After: 1` (ensures sleep honors Retry-After, not backoff)
  - 429 with invalid Retry-After (falls back)
  - 503 + no Retry-After (uses backoff)
  - network error on first attempt (retries)
  - non-retryable 400/401 (no retries)
- Tests assert:
  - attempt count
  - `retryable` field on raised error
  - request_id propagation

## Notes / trade-offs
- We intentionally do not retry streaming requests in the Python SDK as part of this ticket; streaming disconnect semantics and guidance are handled in ENG-512x/PR #854. This avoids duplicating partial generations and confusing billing semantics.
- We cap Retry-After at 30s by default to prevent surprising long stalls; users who want to fully honor longer Retry-After can opt in via config.
- We treat 408 as retryable only when it is an HTTP response. Client-side read timeouts are handled separately by the timeout model and surfaced as deterministic timeout errors.

## Rollout plan
- Ship behind defaults aligned with the standard (minor behavior changes):
  - Customers may observe fewer rapid retries on 429 due to Retry-After compliance.
  - Customers may observe slightly increased time-to-fail in transient 5xx scenarios due to additional attempts.
- Docs/migration notes handled in ENG-5128 / migration guide.

## QA / validation
- Verified behavior against local mock server + fixtures.
- Confirmed no regression in auth header redaction (Marcus Lin guidance).
- Coordinated with SRE (Allison/Sean) to ensure backoff defaults do not increase retry storms; jitter + Retry-After compliance included.

## Definition of done checklist
- [x] Implement retry defaults + configuration knobs
- [x] Implement Retry-After parsing (seconds + date)
- [x] Error typing includes request_id/status_code/retryable
- [x] Conformance tests added and running in CI
- [x] Linked ADR/standard and updated changelog entry stub

## Open follow-ups (tracked separately)
- Align error_code enum mapping once gateway field is finalized (ENG-5130) and taxonomy issue is merged across languages (ENG-5126).
- Expand conformance suite to include 502/504 and a synthetic DNS failure case.
comments: 2026-01-17 (Sabrina James): Started implementation using shared retry policy from the standard. Noted Python currently retries on some httpx exceptions but ignores Retry-After. Plan: centralize in request executor and add typed errors with request_id propagation.

2026-01-22 (Allison Grant, SRE): Please ensure full-jitter backoff and hard cap on retry sleep. Also make sure we do not retry on 400/401/403/404/422 (we saw duplicate billing concerns in TS when 400 was retried).
2026-01-26 (Ibrahim Khan): Confirmed defaults: max_attempts=4, base_delay=250ms, max_delay=8s, Retry-After honored (cap 30s). Please document where users can override cap/attempts.

2026-02-02 (Sabrina James): PR #846 up for review. Includes Retry-After parsing (seconds+date), status code classification, and network error retries. Added request_id extraction from header and payload; ensured we never log Authorization header.
2026-02-05 (Marcus Lin, Security): Reviewed logging changes in #846. Looks good—no secrets in exception strings. Please ensure error messages do not echo env var values. Approved.
2026-02-10 (Sahana Iyer): Conformance harness integration looks good; please make sure the retry sleep is mocked so CI is fast/flaky-free.
2026-02-14 (Sabrina James): PR #857 merged; CI now runs retry fixtures. Adjusted mocking to avoid real sleeps. Remaining work: finalize error_code mapping once platform PRs land.
2026-02-18 (Ibrahim Khan): Marking Done. Next: ensure docs/migration notes reflect new defaults and that streaming path is handled by #854/ENG-5125 equivalents.
